page: Microsoft Azure M32ts is an x86_64 architecture server within the MS family, virtualized via Microsoft Hyper-V. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8280M processor running at 2.7 GHz, delivering 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor includes 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a 38 MB L3 cache, supporting advanced instruction sets such as AVX, AVX-512F, AES, BMI2, ADX, and FMA.

The instance is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, providing 6.0 GB of RAM per core. It includes 1049 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, though it does not bundle any complimentary public IPv4 addresses or GPU hardware.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear tradeoff between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core execution, including stress-ng, Geekbench, and single-threaded compression tasks, falls into the bottom 10% tier. Conversely, multi-core performance, memory bandwidth (both cached and uncached), and database operations consistently register in the middle 50% tier. Redis SET operations reach 20.68 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput achieves 17.69 GB/sec.

This hardware profile is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that benefit from high memory density and multi-threaded execution rather than raw single-core speed. It is appropriate for database operations, multi-threaded decompression, static web serving, and moderate LLM inference tasks using small to medium models, while being less optimal for single-threaded applications or large-scale LLM inference.
